title: Agentic HIL configuration
description: Authoritative Agentic HIL project configuration containing all hardware resources, permissions, and limits. Reading a device needs no permission from version 2 on: exclusivity for the duration of a run replaced the read permission, so allow_probe and allow_read exist only in version 1 files. Writing and state-changing operations are declared per device: on the debugger that may be flashed or reset, and on each COM port and CAN bus that may be written. A generated configuration sets every one of them true, except allow_raw_debugger_commands and allow_mass_erase which it sets false because either one being true refuses flashing on that probe, so the bench is workable without hand-edited YAML. What an agent may write into a permission through project_config_set is false and nothing else, so that call can only ever narrow this file; regenerating it is a separate door with a separate grant (allow_config_write, or agentic-hil init --force at a person's shell) and it writes permissions again from the skeleton and the file it replaces.

debugger_permissions.description: What this debug probe may do beyond reading it. Scoped to this debugger alone, so narrowing one board leaves a second board in the same file untouched. A generated configuration sets allow_flash, allow_reset and allow_debug_execution true and sets allow_raw_debugger_commands and allow_mass_erase false: validated flashing and unrestricted debugger access are mutually exclusive, so either of the latter two being true refuses flash_firmware on this probe and refuses a debug session outright, and neither has a tool behind it to trade for that. A flag a file does not name is false, because absence must not widen a configuration written before this default changed. allow_probe is a version 1 field and is refused in a version 2 file.

allow_probe.description: Version 1 only. Reading a target needs no permission from version 2 on; remove the key and bump version.

allow_debug_execution.description: Whether a debug session on this probe may resume a halted target: debug_continue and nothing else reads this. Opening a session and inspecting one while it is halted need only allow_probe (or, from version 2 on, nothing at all); this is the separate grant for lifting the core off that halt. A flag a file does not name is false, so a configuration written before this permission existed does not gain the ability to resume a target silently on update.

io_permissions.description: What this COM port or CAN bus may do beyond reading it. Scoped to this device alone. A generated configuration sets it true; a flag a file does not name is false, because absence must not widen a configuration written before this default changed. allow_read is a version 1 field and is refused in a version 2 file.

allow_read.description: Version 1 only. Reading a device needs no permission from version 2 on; remove the key and bump version.

version.description: Which rules this file is read under; all three are read, so no file already on disk has to move. Absent means version 1: reading is gated by allow_probe and allow_read, which is how every file written before that release behaves and keeps behaving. Version 2 has no read permission at all; migrating means removing those keys and setting version: 2 in one edit. Version 3 additionally requires every com_ports entry to say which hardware it is - a serial_number, a resource_id, a /dev/serial/by-id/... device name, or an explicit identity_source naming what identifies it instead. `agentic-hil adopt-hardware --apply` fills that in from the attached adapter and is run before the version is raised. A new file should say 3.

workspace_root.description: Absolute path of the workspace this configuration authorizes. It is the runtime working directory.

state_root.description: Absolute operator-controlled directory shared by every frontend for persistent locks, leases, quarantine incidents, and canonical reports. It must be outside workspace_root.

permissions.description: Project-scoped permissions: what may be done to this project beside its hardware. Three of them are about this configuration itself; allow_recover is about this bench's quarantine incidents, and allow_upgrade about the installation serving it. A generated configuration sets every one true. project_config_set writes false into a permission and no other value, so through that call each of these can go from true to false and none of them back. The one MCP call that writes permissions any other way is project_config_create, which regenerates the whole file from hardware discovery under allow_config_write: it carries the permissions of the configuration this server loaded onto the entries that are already there — not the ones on disk, so a narrowing made through project_config_set closes the regeneration path only once the server has been restarted onto it — gives an entry it discovers for the first time the same generated defaults, and generates a file at those defaults when there is none. Separate grants rather than one, so that opening the file far enough for an agent to enter a probe serial does not also hand over the permissions block.

allow_config_write.description: Whether an agent may regenerate this whole configuration from hardware discovery through project_config_create. True in a generated configuration. A regeneration is not the narrowing path and does not obey its ratchet: it carries the permissions of the configuration this server loaded — the state it holds in memory, which a project_config_set narrowing since startup has not changed — onto the entries that are already in the file, and everything else in the file it writes is granted: an entry the discovery finds for the first time, and every entry at all if the configuration has been deleted since. So in one running server a narrow-then-regenerate puts the loaded grant back. Set it false to stop the agent regenerating this file from hardware, and with it refreshing probe ids and COM devices, at all.

allow_config_description_write.description: Whether an agent may change this bench's description field-wise through project_config_set: target.*, debuggers.<name>.type/probe_id/executable/interface_cfg/target_cfg/connect_mode, com_ports.<name>.device/baudrate, and every can_buses.<name> field except its permissions. It never reaches a permission key (no permissions: block, and neither artifacts.allow_upload nor debug.allow_all_symbols), so it decides nothing about what may be done to the hardware. This is the grant for the common case: a board was attached after init and its identity has to be entered.

allow_config_permissions_write.description: Whether an agent may change permissions field-wise through project_config_set. It gates every permission key in the file: each permissions: block, the two grants that sit directly on a section (artifacts.allow_upload and debug.allow_all_symbols), and this key, allow_config_description_write, allow_recover and allow_upgrade themselves. Only false may be written: a change that would turn any permission on is refused as permission_widening_denied, whatever key it named. So this hands over the taking-away, not the granting — with it an agent can narrow this bench on your request, and setting it false itself is the last permission change it can make through project_config_set, after which a regeneration (agentic-hil init --force, or project_config_create while allow_config_write is still true) is what writes permissions into this file again.

allow_recover.description: Whether an agent may clear this bench's quarantine over MCP through hardware_recover. True in a generated configuration. With no argument it reaches only the reasons that name no hardware contact — a lease release that could not persist its own record, an owner that died before its call reached the board, and whatever this bench's recovery.auto_recover policy already lets the automatic path settle. A reason that needs somebody to look at the board (an unconfirmed flash, a death mid-session, cleanup nobody could confirm) needs the tool's operator_statement argument: the confirmation is a claim about the physical world, and no agent may make it, but it may relay one, so such a reason clears over MCP only when the agent passes back an operator_statement a person actually gave it, written to the ledger as their word relayed by the agent — never invented. The audit-broken family clears through neither, keeping the agentic-hil recover --confirm-safe-state command line the refusal carries; so does any case with nobody to ask. Set this false to keep an agent out of incidents entirely, so that every quarantine on this bench waits for a person.

allow_upgrade.description: Whether an agent may replace this installation with the newest release through the server_upgrade MCP tool. True in a generated configuration. The one project permission that is not about this file: it decides whether the main surface can perform the basic maintenance of its own server, which on an MCP host without a shell is otherwise unreachable. The tool takes no version argument at all and can only lift to the newest release, so it is no route around a permission set false here — an agent that could choose a version could install one that reads this file differently. It is refused while a run or a lease holds the bench, it is refused on Windows because the files of a running process are locked there and only the command line can replace them, and after a swap that did happen it reports restart_required: true rather than claiming this server now runs the new code. Set it false to keep upgrading at the command line, where agentic-hil upgrade does the same thing for a person.

provenance.description: Who wrote this file and who last changed it. Informational only: nothing reads it as policy and it grants nothing. It exists so a later reader does not have to guess whether a person intended these contents.

created_by.description: "agent" means an agent generated this file over MCP out of hardware discovery, with every permission true except allow_raw_debugger_commands and allow_mass_erase, which a generation writes false so that flashing works; a regeneration carries over the permissions of the configuration that server had loaded instead.

created_via.description: The interface that wrote it, e.g. mcp:project_config_create.

created_at.description: UTC ISO-8601 timestamp of the write.

last_modified_by.description: Who made the most recent field-wise change. Written by project_config_set: "agent" when the change came over MCP, "human" when a person ran a command such as agentic-hil adopt-hardware. Editing this file by hand leaves it as it was, which is itself the signal that the recorded change is not the newest one.

last_modified_via.description: The call that made the most recent change, e.g. mcp:project_config_set or cli:adopt-hardware.

last_modified_at.description: UTC ISO-8601 timestamp of the most recent field-wise change.

last_modified_keys.description: The dotted keys the most recent field-wise change set, so a later reader sees what moved and not only that something did.

modification_count.description: How many field-wise changes have been applied to this file. A count rather than a log: an unbounded history inside the policy file itself would grow without limit, and the count is what tells a reader whether last_modified_keys is the whole story.

debuggers.description: Named debug probes. The name is the routing key: test plan steps address a probe by it, and each probe carries its own permissions. Once several are configured every entry needs its own probe_id — it is the only field that selects a physical probe, and resource_id merely aliases the coordination lease, so it never substitutes for one.

type.description: Which debug stack drives this probe. It is part of the bench description and is settable behind allow_config_description_write, beside executable, interface_cfg and target_cfg, which already decide which binary runs with which scripts. A change to it is refused unless the entry that comes out of the call carries what the named backend requires and this surface can write: switching to openocd needs interface_cfg and target_cfg, so a backend switch lands whole or not at all. Send executable in the same call too, or null to have the new backend's binary discovered, because an executable already in the entry was chosen for the backend the entry is leaving.

connect_mode.description: How the probe attaches to the target for a flash. hotplug connects to the running core, which is what every configuration written before this key existed does and what the default keeps doing. under_reset holds the target in reset while the connection is made, which is the remedy for a core that runs from flash and defeats the erase; it needs the probe's reset line wired to the target's NRST (an on-board ST-Link has it). Read by the stlink backend only, where it selects STM32CubeProgrammer's mode=HOTPLUG or mode=UR for the flash command; probe_target keeps connecting hot plug so it stays the least intrusive call, and reset_target keeps its own NORMAL connect. openocd and pyocd refuse under_reset at load rather than ignoring it.

timeout_s.description: Seconds one debugger operation may take before it is abandoned. Greater than zero, not merely non-negative: the value reaches the backend as the subprocess wait, and at zero it has already expired when the probe is asked for, so every probe, flash and reset fails as a timeout against hardware that was never given a chance to answer.

target.description: Per-debugger target override for a probe on a second board; unspecified fields default to the top-level target.

debug.description: Typed debug-session settings for safe GDB/OpenOCD operations.

allowed_roots.description: Directories under workspace_root that firmware may be flashed from and debug dumps written to, each including its subdirectories. A single "." is the whole workspace, recursively, and is what a generated configuration names; list directories instead to narrow it. Omitting the key means ["build"], which is what configurations written before 0.8.0 mean and never changes under them. An empty list is refused rather than read as either "everything" or "nothing". This list never relaxes containment in workspace_root, the extension list, or the format check.

com_ports.description: Named serial/COM ports that Agentic HIL may open for stimuli and feedback. Reading needs no permission; assert_dtr and assert_rts decide whether opening the port touches the target.

device.description: How the port is opened. On Linux prefer the stable /dev/serial/by-id/... symlink, which names the vendor, the product and the device's own serial number: /dev/ttyACM0 is an enumeration order, so attaching a second adapter can hand one board the name the other had. Windows has no openable stable name — COMn is all there is — so name the port there and let serial_number carry the identity.

serial_number.description: The USB serial number of the adapter behind this port, which on a Nucleo is the ST-Link serial that probe_id also carries. This is the port's identity; device is only the way in. Set, it becomes the machine-wide lock key, and it is compared against the attached hardware when the port is opened so an entry that has come to name a different board is refused rather than used. Unset, the entry is identified by its kernel name alone. `agentic-hil adopt-hardware` fills it in from the attached probe.

vid.description: The USB vendor id of the adapter behind this port. Two spellings, both accepted and normalised to the integer on load: a number is decimal, which is what pyserial reports and what adopt-hardware writes (1155), and a quoted value is the hexadecimal lsusb prints, with or without the 0x marker ("0483", "0x0483"). Unlike serial_number this names a device type rather than a unit, so it is never a lock key — what it buys is that a USB serial is unique only within a vendor, so a matching serial under a foreign vid/pid is refused at open, and an adapter that publishes no serial at all still gets a named type check.

pid.description: The USB product id of the adapter behind this port, alongside vid and spelled the same two ways: decimal as a number (14159), hexadecimal in quotes ("374f"). Optional and independent of vid; each one set is compared against the attached device when the port is opened.

assert_dtr.description: Whether DTR is asserted when the port is opened. pyserial asserts it by default, and on boards that wire DTR to reset that restarts the target on every open. Set false to observe a target provably undisturbed; leave true when the peer needs DTR to talk.

assert_rts.description: Whether RTS is asserted when the port is opened. Same reasoning as assert_dtr; some boards wire RTS to reset or boot mode.

identity_source.description: Which key of this entry says which hardware it is, written down. It grants nothing and identifies nothing on its own: a value that disagrees with the entry's own keys is refused at load, so it can only ever repeat what serial_number, resource_id and vid/pid already say. What it buys is a file in which "identified by a type, because this adapter publishes no serial number" and "nobody got round to it" are different sentences - which is why version 3 requires it on any entry carrying no serial_number, no resource_id and no /dev/serial/by-id/... device name. `vid_pid` (or `vid`/`pid`) is the deliberate exception for an adapter that publishes USB ids but no serial; `device` states that this port is identified by its kernel name and nothing else. `agentic-hil adopt-hardware --apply` writes whichever the attached adapter turns out to justify.

can_buses.description: Named CAN buses that Agentic HIL may open for stimuli and feedback.

listen_only.description: Whether this bus is observed without sending dominant ACK bits. Enforced per adapter rather than assumed: peak sets PCAN's passive state and reads the parameter back from the driver, socketcan reads the kernel's control mode because only `ip link` can set it, and a process bridge must confirm the mode in its open response. An adapter that cannot be held to it refuses the session with can_listen_only_unsupported or can_listen_only_unconfirmed instead of listening anyway.

max_frame_data_bytes.description: Maximum CAN payload size in bytes. Defaults to 8, or 64 when fd is true. Capped at 8 unless fd is true: classic CAN cannot carry more, whatever this is set to.

listen_only_enforcement.description: What listen_only above is worth on this bus. `controller` is the per-controller proof the adapter itself provides. `service` is the CAN broker filtering frames in software for the participants attached to it, which is a weaker and different claim: it is reported as software filtering wherever it is reported, and never as the controller proof.

shares.description: Named participant views of this physical bus. Present means the bus is brokered: one process owns the adapter and holds the machine-wide bus lock, and runs attach to a named share instead of racing for the device. Absent - the default - means the single-owner bus this project has always had, unchanged.

filter.description: Identifier acceptance terms. A frame reaches this participant, and may be sent by it, when (frame_id & mask) == (id & mask) for any term. An empty list accepts every identifier.

max_frames.description: Frame budget for one attachment of this participant. Exhausting it aborts that participant's run and leaves the bus and the other participants running.

requires_listen_only.description: Whether this view is only meaningful while nothing on the bus transmits. Such a participant and a participant with allow_write cannot be attached at the same time; the refusal names the bus listen_only_enforcement level.

recovery.description: How far the owning process may clear its own hardware quarantines before an operator is required.

auto_recover.description: off: only an operator clears a quarantine. readonly: reap this owner's debugger processes and re-read the probe, touching nothing physical. reset_halt: additionally drive a reset-into-halt to settle an unconfirmed flash or reset. Use readonly on a bench whose peripherals react to a reset.

max_attempts.description: Machine recovery attempts allowed per quarantine incident before the owner stops trying and defers to an operator.
